question: Does simpler 3- or 4-parameter learned write gain outperform strong calibrated nonlearned adaptive update strategies on an independently seeded nonstationary causal-memory DEV source at exactly 256 persistent floats per world?

hypotheses.primary: Three-parameter magnitude-only learned controller improves VAL query MSE by >=10% against best of all fixed adaptive/constant comparators, for each of 3 independent seeds, while stable-role error <=1.05x best fixed stable and changed-role error <=0.9x best fixed changed.
hypotheses.direction: Four-parameter cosine gain improves changed-role VAL error >=10% vs otherwise identical three-parameter controller and stable error <=1.05x three-parameter in all three seeds.
hypotheses.null: A properly calibrated fixed rule is as good or better than learned on fresh VAL; no directional contribution at the preregistered effect threshold.
